heading: The last house Luis Barragán designed
html: Casa Meyer was drawn in October 1978 for Barbara Meyer, on a hillside street in Bosques de las Lomas, Mexico City. From the street it is a long white wall under a hedge of vines, with one yellow gate. It remains a private home.

photo.alt: The street facade of Casa Meyer with its yellow gate

heading: A gift between friends
html: Barbara Meyer and Luis Barragán were friends for nearly twenty-five years. At seventy-six, with his office all but closed, he designed one last house for her and dedicated the drawings in his own hand: para Baby Meyer de Garate, con todo cariño.

heading: Luis Barragán, 1902–1988
html: The most prominent figure in modern Mexican architecture built little, almost all of it in and around Mexico City: houses, gardens, a chapel, stables, towers. He spoke of serenity, silence and solitude as the qualities a house should offer.

heading: Visit the house
html: Small groups are received on selected days, by appointment. A visit follows the sequence of walls, light and colour as Barragán laid it out, from the yellow gate through the house to the garden.
